# Scientific writing

Identify the document type, audience, purpose, venue, evidence sources, and requested scope. Read only the relevant project files.

## Workflow
1. Build a claim-evidence outline before drafting substantial text.
2. Use current code, outputs, figures, decision records, and verified literature as sources of truth.
3. Distinguish methods, observations, results, interpretation, and speculation.
4. Keep claims proportional to the study design and uncertainty.
5. Apply the reporting guideline appropriate to the actual study type when relevant.
6. Preserve terminology, units, sample definitions, and figure references across sections.
7. Flag missing evidence, unresolved contradictions, and statements requiring author judgment.

For methods or results, invoke the dedicated skill and apply its DVC freshness and manuscript evidence-map rules. Never invent citations, methods, numerical results, ethical approvals, software versions, or completed validation.
